formation.title: The Sultanate Restored
formation.text:
The banner of the Seljuks flies once more over the heartland of Anatolia. Where once a dozen beyliks squabbled over the carcass of the old sultanate, a single sovereign now commands the allegiance of all Turkic lords from the Black Sea to the Mediterranean. The caravanserais that line the ancient roads stand ready to channel the wealth of nations, while the ghulam cavalry that once rode at the Sultan's side awaits a new master's call.

The question now is what manner of realm this restored sultanate shall become. Shall it follow the path of the warrior-sultans who once made the Crusaders tremble and the Byzantines flee, projecting military power across two seas? Or shall it embrace its destiny as the great crossroads of civilization, where Persian poetry, Greek philosophy, and Turkic valor meet in the bazaars and medreses of Konya and Kayseri?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: We are the Sultan of Two Seas!

modifiers.name: Sultan of Two Seas
modifiers.text: As Alaeddin Keykubat once ruled from the Mediterranean to the Black Sea, so too shall the Sultanate of Rum project its power across both coasts of Anatolia. Our cavalry shall thunder across the plateaus and our galleys command the straits.

options.text: We are the Crossroads of Civilizations!

modifiers.name: Crossroads of Civilizations
modifiers.text: Anatolia has always stood at the meeting point of East and West. The Sultanate of Rum shall embrace this heritage, welcoming merchants from every land and scholars from every tradition, building a realm where commerce and culture flourish together.

advances.name: Ghulam Cavalry Tradition
advances.text: The Seljuk practice of training elite slave soldiers, the ghulams, into a disciplined cavalry force loyal only to the Sultan. Drawn from captured youths and trained in horsemanship and combat, these warriors formed the backbone of the Seljuk royal guard.

advances.name: Caravanserai Network
advances.text: The Seljuks built over a hundred caravanserais across Anatolia, spaced one day's journey apart along trade routes. These fortified waypoints offered free lodging, food, and medical care to all travelers for three days: a remarkable system of trade infrastructure.

advances.name: Turkmen Raiders
advances.text: The semi-nomadic Turkmen tribes who formed the vanguard of Seljuk expansion. Fast, fearless, and adept at hit-and-run tactics, they served as the frontier raiders and scouts of the sultanate.

advances.name: Iqta Land Grant System
advances.text: The Seljuk system of granting revenue rights over land parcels to military commanders in exchange for cavalry service. This timar-like arrangement ensured a ready supply of mounted warriors without maintaining a permanent standing army.

advances.name: Medrese Foundations
advances.text: The great medreses of Konya, Kayseri, and Sivas, institutions of Islamic learning that preserved and transmitted knowledge in theology, law, medicine, and mathematics during the Seljuk golden age.

advances.name: Seljuk Administrative Tradition
advances.text: The Persian-influenced bureaucratic system inherited from the Great Seljuk Empire, with its divan councils, viziers, and provincial governance structures that maintained order across Anatolia's diverse populations.

advances.name: Frontier Beylik Warriors
advances.text: The uc beyleri, frontier lords who maintained garrisons along the Byzantine border. Their warriors, hardened by constant skirmishing, served as the first line of defense and the spearhead of expansion.

advances.name: Ahi Brotherhood Guilds
advances.text: The remarkable Ahi brotherhoods that combined Sufi spirituality with artisan craftsmanship. Founded by Ahi Evran in the 13th century, these guilds organized craftsmen, regulated trade, provided social services, and even maintained armed militias for urban defense.

event.title: The Ahi Brotherhood Reborn
event.text: The workshops of our cities have come alive with a spirit not seen since the days of Ahi Evran himself. The Ahi brotherhoods, those remarkable guilds that blended Sufi devotion with honest craftsmanship, have reorganized under our patronage. From tanners to coppersmiths, from weavers to blacksmiths, the artisans of Anatolia bind themselves by oaths of brotherhood, fair dealing, and mutual aid. Their zaviyes serve as hostelries for travelers, their councils settle disputes without recourse to courts, and their young apprentices train in arms as well as craft, ready to defend the cities that sustain them.

options.text: Let the guilds flourish under our protection.

modifiers.name: Revival of the Ahi Brotherhood
modifiers.text: The Ahi guilds have been reinvigorated, their workshops humming with productivity and their principles of honest trade and mutual aid spreading through the cities of Anatolia.

options.text: Let the brotherhoods bind our communities together.

modifiers.name: Guild Solidarity
modifiers.text: The Ahi brotherhoods bind communities together through shared craft, mutual aid, and armed civic defense: a network of solidarity that strengthens the social fabric of the realm.

advances.name: Alanya Shipyard
advances.text: The great naval arsenal at Alanya, built in 1227 by Sultan Alaeddin Keykubat. Carved into the rocky peninsula beneath the Red Tower, its five vaulted galleries allowed ships to be built and launched directly into the Mediterranean.

event.title: The Shipyards of the Two Seas
event.text: The great shipyard at Alanya, carved into the rock face of the Red Tower peninsula, echoes once more with the sound of hammer and saw. Built by Sultan Alaeddin Keykubat to project Seljuk power across the Mediterranean, this remarkable structure, five vaulted galleries open to the sea, now launches vessels bearing our standard. Together with the naval facilities at Sinop on the Black Sea, our realm commands the coastlines that the Seljuk sultans of old named their twin domains. The Sultan of Two Seas is no longer merely a title.

options.text: Our galleys shall command both seas.

advances.name: Mevlevi Order
advances.text: The Sufi order founded by the followers of Mevlana Jalaluddin Rumi in Konya. Known for their whirling dervish ceremony (sema), the Mevlevi became one of the most influential spiritual movements in the Islamic world.

event.title: The Whirling Dervishes of Konya
event.text: In the tekke at Konya, the followers of Mevlana Jalaluddin Rumi continue the sublime practice of the sema: the whirling dance that brings the devotee closer to the divine. The Mevlevi Order has become the spiritual heart of our realm, attracting poets, scholars, and mystics from across the Islamic world. Their message of universal love and tolerance has softened the edges of sectarian conflict and inspired a flowering of Persian literature and music that brings prestige to the Sultanate of Rum far beyond what armies alone could achieve.

options.text: The dervishes bring wisdom and harmony to our realm.

modifiers.name: Legacy of Mevlana
modifiers.text: The teachings of Mevlana Rumi echo through the tekkes and medreses of Rum, inspiring a tolerance and spiritual depth that draws seekers from across the Islamic world.

options.text: Their libraries and schools are the true treasure.

modifiers.name: Mevlevi Scholarship
modifiers.text: The Mevlevi libraries and schools attract scholars and poets from across the Islamic world, making the Sultanate a center of learning and artistic achievement.

advances.name: Darüşşifa
advances.text: The Seljuk tradition of building hospitals (darüşşifas) attached to mosque complexes. These institutions provided medical care to all, regardless of faith or wealth, and advanced medical knowledge through practical treatment.

advances.name: Turco-Persian Court Culture
advances.text: The refined court culture of the Sultanate of Rum, where Persian was the language of poetry and administration, Arabic the language of religion, and Turkish the language of the military: a trilingual civilization of remarkable sophistication.

advances.name: Anatolian Silk Trade
advances.text: The silk production and trade that flourished in Anatolia under Seljuk patronage, with Bursa and other cities becoming major centers of silk weaving that supplied markets across the Mediterranean. The looms stand in the halls of the Ahi guilds.

advances.name: Sipahi Cavalry
advances.text: The professional cavalry force supported by the timar land-grant system. Sipahis were required to maintain horses, equipment, and retainers in exchange for revenue from their assigned lands: a feudal military system that produced formidable mounted warriors.

advances.name: Composite Bow Tradition
advances.text: The Turkic mastery of the composite bow: a weapon of horn, wood, and sinew that could be used from horseback or on foot. This tradition of archery excellence gave Anatolian armies a decisive advantage at range.

advances.name: Grand Bazaar
advances.text: The covered marketplaces of the great Anatolian cities, where hundreds of shops offered goods from across the known world. These bustling commercial centers served as the economic heart of the sultanate.

advances.name: Dhimmi Tolerance
advances.text: The Seljuk policy of relative tolerance toward Christian, Jewish, and other non-Muslim communities. Greek artisans, Armenian merchants, and Georgian soldiers all found places within the sultanate's diverse society.

advances.name: Anatolian Carpet Tradition
advances.text: The distinctive carpet weaving traditions of Anatolia, which blended Central Asian nomadic patterns with settled workshop techniques to create some of the most prized textiles in the world. The guild halls of the towns take up the craft.

advances.name: Anatolian Fortress Tradition
advances.text: The network of castles and fortifications built across Anatolia's mountainous terrain, from the citadels of Ankara and Konya to the coastal fortresses at Alanya and Sinop.

advances.name: Two Seas Port System
advances.text: The development of port facilities on both the Mediterranean and Black Sea coasts, fulfilling the Seljuk ambition to be the Sultan of Two Seas and controlling maritime trade along both coastlines.

advances.name: Azab Light Infantry
advances.text: Light auxiliary infantry drawn from the peasant population, the azabs served as garrison troops, siege auxiliaries, and expendable screens for the more valuable cavalry. Their large numbers compensated for their lesser equipment.

advances.name: Gunpowder Arsenal
advances.text: The establishment of arsenals for the production and storage of gunpowder weapons (cannons, bombards, and later firearms) marking the transition from purely cavalry-based warfare to combined-arms tactics.

advances.name: Trade Insurance System
advances.text: The Seljuk innovation of state-backed trade insurance, where the treasury compensated merchants for goods lost to banditry or accident on the road. This remarkable system encouraged long-distance trade by reducing risk.

advances.name: Anatolian Copper Works
advances.text: The exploitation of Anatolia's rich copper deposits, particularly around Kastamonu and Tokat, which supplied raw material for the distinctive Seljuk metalwork tradition of engraved copper vessels and decorative arts. The coppersmiths work in the halls of the Ahi guilds.

advances.name: Waqf Endowment System
advances.text: The system of charitable endowments (waqf) that funded medreses, hospitals, caravanserais, and soup kitchens. These pious foundations provided a stable source of income for public institutions outside the direct control of the state.

advances.name: Akinci Raiders
advances.text: The akinci, irregular light cavalry who served as the advance guard and raiding force of the Sultanate. Operating ahead of the main army, they scouted enemy territory, disrupted supply lines, and spread terror through rapid, devastating raids.

advances.name: Imperial Administration
advances.text: The centralization of provincial governance under appointed officials, replacing the semi-autonomous beylik system with a more unified administrative structure befitting an empire.

advances.name: Nizam-i Jedid
advances.text: The New Order, disciplined infantry trained along Western European lines, equipped with modern firearms and drill. This reform sought to create a professional standing army to replace the increasingly unreliable traditional forces.

advances.name: State Manufactories
advances.text: Centralized production facilities established under state direction, producing textiles, weapons, and other goods for both domestic consumption and export: an early attempt at state-led industrialization.

advances.name: Centralized Tax Reform
advances.text: The abolition of tax farming and the establishment of direct tax collection by salaried officials, increasing state revenue and reducing the exploitation of peasants by intermediary tax collectors.

advances.name: Angora Mohair Industry
advances.text: The processing of mohair from the Angora goats native to central Anatolia: a luxury fiber prized across Europe for its lustrous sheen and softness, providing a lucrative export commodity.

advances.name: Naval Modernization
advances.text: The modernization of the Sultanate's naval capabilities, building upon the Seljuk tradition of the Alanya and Sinop shipyards to create a fleet capable of projecting power in the Mediterranean.

advances.name: Kırlangıç Squadrons
advances.text: The adoption of the kırlangıç, the swallow of the Ottoman fleet: a fast, lateen-rigged Mediterranean vessel ideal for both commerce raiding and coastal patrol. Light and maneuverable, it could outrun heavier European warships.

advances.name: Modern Anatolian Army
advances.text: The final transformation of the Sultanate's military into a modern force, professional officers, standardized equipment, and modern tactics replacing the last vestiges of the medieval military tradition.

advances.name: Anatolian Railway
advances.text: The construction of railway lines connecting the cities of Anatolia, binding the realm together with iron rails and enabling rapid movement of troops and goods across the plateau.

advances.name: Constitutional Reform
advances.text: The introduction of constitutional principles limiting royal authority and establishing consultative bodies: a modernizing reform that sought to strengthen the state through shared governance.

advances.name: Universal Conscription
advances.text: The introduction of mandatory military service for all male subjects, creating a mass army that drew upon the entire population rather than relying on professional soldiers and feudal levies alone.

advances.name: Anatolian National Awakening
advances.text: The emergence of a modern national consciousness among the peoples of Anatolia, driven by the printing press, public education, and a growing sense of shared identity transcending tribal and regional loyalties.

advances.name: Anatolian Mining Industry
advances.text: The industrial exploitation of Anatolia's mineral wealth: chromite, iron, and copper deposits that would become strategically vital resources in the age of modern industry. The ores of the plateau are brought to the furnaces of the state manufactories and made into steel.

destiny.name: Destiny of Rum
destiny.text: The Sultanate has been restored. Now choose the path that will define its legacy: will you project power across two seas, or build the greatest crossroads of civilization the world has known?

event.title: The Destiny of Rum
event.text: The Sultanate of Rum stands restored and stable, its lands united under a single sovereign. The ancient roads of Anatolia carry merchants and soldiers alike, and the medreses hum with scholarship. The realm's destiny now unfolds before us.

destiny.name: Command the Coasts
destiny.text: Secure the gateway cities that guard Anatolia's frontiers. Aleppo opens the road to Syria and the Levant, while Edirne commands the passage into Europe. With these anchors held, the Sultan of Two Seas begins to earn his title.

conditions.text: Own Aleppo, or a subject owns it
Own Edirne, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Coasts Secured
event.text: The banner of the Sultanate flies over Aleppo and Edirne. From the minarets of Syria to the walls of Thrace, the Sultan's authority extends beyond the Anatolian heartland. The coastlines of the Mediterranean and the Black Sea lie open to our ambitions, and the title Sultan of Two Seas takes on new meaning.

options.text: The seas shall know our name.

destiny.name: Master of the Straits
destiny.text: The city of Constantine and the seat of the Abbasid caliphs must both bow to the Sultan's banner. Constantinople commands the straits between Europe and Asia, while Baghdad anchors the eastern reaches of the Islamic world.

conditions.text: Own Constantinople, or a subject owns it
Own Baghdad, or a subject owns it

event.title: Master of the Straits
event.text: Constantinople and Baghdad have fallen to our armies. The city of emperors and the city of caliphs now answer to the Sultan of Rum. This dual conquest echoes the ambitions of the greatest Islamic empires: shall we embrace the ghazi warrior spirit that won these cities, or forge a professional imperial guard worthy of ruling them?

options.text: The ghazi spirit burns in our hearts.

modifiers.name: Spirit of the Ghazi
modifiers.text: The holy warrior tradition of the frontier ghazis fuels our armies with righteous fervor, enabling them to recover quickly and fight with tireless determination.

options.text: An imperial guard shall defend our conquests.

modifiers.name: Imperial Guard
modifiers.text: A professional imperial guard ensures military efficiency on land and sea, though maintaining such an elite force strains the treasury.

destiny.name: Sultan of Sultans
destiny.text: The ultimate aspiration of Turkic sovereignty: to hold Cairo, Tabriz, and Mecca under one banner. The ruler who commands the Nile, the Caspian frontier, and the Holy Cities of Islam may rightly claim the title Sultan of Sultans.

conditions.text: Own Cairo, or a subject owns it
Own Tabrīz, or a subject owns it
Own Mecca, or a subject owns it

event.title: Sultan of Sultans
event.text: Cairo, Tabriz, and Mecca bow before our throne. The Nile's wealth, the Caspian frontier's strength, and the spiritual authority of the Holy Cities all converge in our realm. No sultan in the Islamic world commands such power or prestige. Shall we claim the universal sovereignty this position demands, or establish a lasting peace across the lands of Islam?

modifiers.name: Universal Sultan
modifiers.text: The claim of universal sovereignty over the Islamic world commands the loyalty of subjects and the respect of rivals, though imperial ambition drives construction costs ever higher.

options.text: Let us build a Pax Islamica.

modifiers.name: Pax Islamica
modifiers.text: The Sultan's peace extends across the lands of Islam, enabling devastated regions to recover, diverse peoples to integrate, and intelligence networks to reach every corner of the realm.

destiny.name: Silk Road Revival
destiny.text: Anatolia sits at the western terminus of the ancient Silk Road. By raising caravanserais along the roads, as the Seljuk sultans did, and ensuring silk flows through the capital market, the Sultanate can restore itself as the great commercial bridge between East and West.

children.text: Silk is produced in the market
Silk is traded in the market

conditions.text: Has a Caravanserai in at least 4 locations

event.title: The Silk Road Revived
event.text: The caravanserais that dot the Anatolian landscape once more bustle with merchants bearing silk from the East. Our moneychangers extend credit, our bazaars overflow with exotic goods, and the name of Rum is spoken with respect in trading houses from Venice to Samarkand. The old Silk Road lives again, with our cities at its heart.

options.text: The wealth of nations flows through our hands.

destiny.name: Emporium of the East
destiny.text: The markets of Rum overflow with the riches of the world. Saffron from the Anatolian highlands joins silk, copper, and wool in bazaars that rival any in the world. Sivas, where the road from Tabriz meets the roads to Sinop and the Cilician ports, is held and grown into the emporium it was under the Seljuk sultans.

conditions.text: A market the country is in

children.text: Saffron is produced in the market
Saffron is traded in the market

conditions.text: Sivas is owned and has at least 29 development

event.title: The Great Emporium
event.text: The markets of Rum have grown beyond mere way-stations on the Silk Road. Saffron, silk, wool, and copper pass through our bazaars in quantities that astonish foreign visitors. Our merchants have become powers unto themselves. Shall we empower these merchant princes to extend our commercial reach, or nurture the bazaar economy that makes our cities the envy of the world?

modifiers.name: Merchant Princes of Rum
modifiers.text: The great merchants of the Sultanate wield influence rivaling that of nobles, expanding diplomatic reach and trade revenue, though their commercial priorities sometimes divert resources from military supply.

options.text: The bazaars are the heart of our wealth.

modifiers.name: Bazaar Economy
modifiers.text: The vibrant bazaar economy of Anatolia drives raw material production, builds naval tradition through coastal commerce, and gives our fleets the experience to enforce trade at sea.

destiny.name: Light of Anatolia
destiny.text: The Sultanate stands at the pinnacle of civilization: a realm where scientific inquiry, artistic achievement, and commercial prosperity have merged into something greater than any of its parts. Medreses stand in five of its towns and hospitals that teach medicine in two of its cities. Konya, the capital of the Seljuk sultans and the city of Mevlana, is held and built up to twice what it was. The Light of Anatolia shines across the world.

conditions.text: Has a Darüşşifa or a Hospital in at least 2 locations
Konya is owned and has at least 46 development

event.title: The Light of Anatolia
event.text: The Sultanate of Rum stands as a beacon of civilization. Our scholars advance human knowledge, our artisans create works of enduring beauty, and our merchants connect the peoples of the world. Shall this flowering take the form of a great cultural and spiritual renaissance, or shall we build an empire of caravans that binds the continents together through trade?

options.text: Let Anatolia's wisdom illuminate the world.

modifiers.name: Anatolian Renaissance
modifiers.text: A great cultural and spiritual flowering transforms the Sultanate, drawing the faithful to its lodges and medreses, expanding governance capacity, and hardening the realm's defenses.

options.text: The caravans shall bind the world together.

modifiers.name: Caravan Empire
modifiers.text: A continental trade network that bridges faiths and civilizations, reducing the cost of wars across religious boundaries while enriching the merchant class and projecting naval power.

units.name: Ghulam Cavalry
units.text: Elite slave cavalry loyal only to the Sultan. Captured as youths and trained in horsemanship and combat from childhood, the ghulams formed the most disciplined and reliable cavalry force in the Seljuk army.

units.name: Turkmen Raider
units.text: Semi-nomadic Turkmen light cavalry, masters of the steppe raiding tradition. Fast, elusive, and expert horsemen, they strike without warning and vanish before the enemy can respond.

units.name: Uc Warrior
units.text: Frontier garrison infantry from the border marches (uc). Hardened by constant skirmishing with Byzantine and Crusader forces, these warriors are tough, resourceful, and accustomed to fighting outnumbered.

units.name: Seljuk War Galley
units.text: A heavy war galley built in the Alanya shipyard tradition. Sturdier and faster than standard galleys, these vessels carry the Sultan's banner across the Mediterranean and Black Sea alike.

units.name: Sipahi
units.text: Professional heavy cavalry supported by the timar land-grant system. Each sipahi maintains his own warhorses, arms, and retainers: a feudal knight of the Turkic world, formidable in both shock charge and pursuit.

units.name: Composite Bow Archer
units.text: Infantry armed with the powerful Turkic composite bow, capable of launching devastating volleys at ranges that European crossbowmen struggle to match. Their rapid rate of fire and mobility make them lethal in open terrain.

units.name: Azab
units.text: Light auxiliary infantry levied from the peasant population. Though lightly equipped, the azabs serve as expendable screens, garrison troops, and siege laborers, freeing the professional cavalry for decisive engagements.

units.name: Akinci Raider
units.text: Irregular light cavalry who ride ahead of the main army, raiding deep into enemy territory. Their speed, ferocity, and skill at living off the land make them the terror of frontier populations and the bane of enemy logistics.

units.name: Nizam-i Jedid
units.text: Soldiers of the New Order, disciplined infantry drilled in European-style tactics, equipped with modern muskets and bayonets. They represent the cutting edge of military reform in the Sultanate.

units.name: Kırlangıç
units.text: A fast, lateen-rigged Mediterranean vessel equally suited to commerce raiding and naval patrol. Light and maneuverable, the kırlangıç can outrun most warships and outfight most merchantmen.

units.name: Modern Anatolian Infantry
units.text: Professional soldiers of the modern Sultanate, equipped with rifled muskets and trained in contemporary European tactics. The culmination of decades of military reform.

units.name: Anatolian Conscript
units.text: Soldiers drawn from across Anatolia through universal conscription. Though less experienced than professional troops, their sheer numbers and fighting spirit make them a formidable force.

buildings.name: Caravanserai
buildings.text: A fortified roadside inn offering shelter, food, and medical care to passing merchants and travelers. The Seljuks built over a hundred of these across Anatolia, each spaced one day's journey apart.

buildings.name: Medrese
buildings.text: An Islamic institution of higher learning, teaching theology, law, medicine, and mathematics. The great medreses of Konya and Kayseri were renowned centers of scholarship in the medieval Islamic world.

buildings.name: Ahi Guild Hall
buildings.text: The meeting hall and workshop of an Ahi brotherhood, part guild hall, part Sufi lodge, part militia armory. Here artisans learn their craft, settle disputes, and maintain the social fabric of the city.

buildings.name: Darüşşifa
buildings.text: The Seljuk tradition of building hospitals (darüşşifas) attached to mosque complexes. These institutions provided medical care to all, regardless of faith or wealth, and advanced medical knowledge through practical treatment.

buildings.name: Grand Bazaar
buildings.text: A covered marketplace where hundreds of shops offer goods from across the known world. The economic heart of the city, where silk, spice, copper, and carpet meet the buyer's purse.

buildings.name: Port Warehouse
buildings.text: Coastal storage and docking facilities supporting the Sultanate's maritime commerce. Goods are loaded and unloaded under the watchful eye of the harbor master.

buildings.name: Gunpowder Arsenal
buildings.text: A military facility for the production and storage of cannons, muskets, and gunpowder. The arsenal marks the transition to modern warfare in the Sultanate.

buildings.name: State Manufactory
buildings.text: A state-directed production facility producing textiles, metalwork, and other goods for domestic use and export.

buildings.name: Railway Station
buildings.text: A station along the new railway lines binding the cities of Anatolia together. Iron rails carry goods, soldiers, and ideas across the plateau at unprecedented speed.

buildings.name: Imperial Divan
buildings.text: The supreme council of the Sultan of Sultans, where the fate of empires is decided. This grand hall of governance projects the authority of universal sovereignty across the Islamic world.

buildings.name: House of Wisdom
buildings.text: An academy of learning that gathers scholars, translators, and scientists from across the known world, reviving the spirit of the great Abbasid Bayt al-Hikma in the heart of Anatolia.

list.name: Divan-ı Âlâ
list.text: The great council of the sultans of Rum, held again as it was at Konya. The vizier presides as sahib-i divan. Beside him sit the müstevfi who keeps the accounts, the tuğrai who draws the sultan's cipher, the müşrif who inspects, the arız who musters the army and the pervane who registers every grant of land. Petitions from the provinces are heard here, and the beys who once ruled alone now wait on its decisions.

list.name: Gulamhane
list.text: The school of the palace slaves, as the Seljuk sultans kept it. Boys taken in war or bought on the frontier, many of them Greek, are converted and raised in the palace as the sultan's own men. They fill his guard and his household offices and some rise to govern, as Celaleddin Karatay did. They owe nothing to any Turkmen house, and the Turkmen houses know it.

list.name: Pervane
list.text: The officer of the great divan who keeps the register of every grant of revenue made to a horseman, and seals its deed. A grant is held for service under arms, it is not inherited, and it is struck from the register when its holder fails the muster. While the register is kept the horsemen ride when called and their districts answer to the sultan. When it is not, grants pass from father to son and become lordships.

list.name: Kadı'l-kudat
list.text: The chief judge of the sultanate, seated at Konya. He names the kadı of every town and stands over the teachers of the medreses that the Seljuk viziers built at Konya, Kayseri and Sivas. His ruling gives the sultan's acts their lawfulness, and a learned man of any town can rise through his courts and schools without the favor of a bey.

list.name: Vakıf Network
list.text: The charitable endowment, an irrevocable trust by which a sultan, a vizier or a princess sets aside the income of villages and shops for ever. The Seljuks of Rum endowed hospitals at Kayseri and Divriği, medreses at Konya and Sivas, and hans a day's march apart on the caravan roads, where any traveler is lodged and fed for three days. What is endowed is lost to the treasury and can not be taken back.

list.name: Mukataa
list.text: The farming of revenue. The right to collect what a district owes is sold for a sum paid in advance, and the buyer keeps whatever more he can raise. Anatolia was governed this way under the Ilkhans, when the great men of Konya bid for whole provinces. The treasury has its coin at once, and the village pays for the bidder's profit.

list.name: Zimmet
list.text: The covenant of protection as the sultans of Rum kept it. The Greek and Armenian towns of Anatolia keep their bishops and their churches, settle suits among themselves before their own clergy, and pay the cizye through their own headmen. A rock church in Cappadocia names the sultan beside the emperor in its dedication. The communities stay loyal and stay apart.
